name: Spare Work
summary: A trades and freelance marketplace run for the people who do the work, who vote on its fees and rules. Customers post a job once and get free quotes, each stage's payment is held until it is signed off, licences are checked against public registers, and workers keep everything except the at-cost fee.

areas.name: Sign-up and accounts
areas.summary: One Spareware login with a customer side and a worker side, plus business accounts for companies, landlords and property managers who hire often.

features.name: Sign up as a customer
features.does: A person can sign up with a passkey or email and post their first job within minutes.

parts.name: Customer sign-up flow
parts.what: Spare Work's short sign-up on the kit's sign-up flow, asking only what a first job needs.

parts.name: Post first, confirm after
parts.what: A customer can write a job first and confirm their account at the end, without losing the draft.

parts.name: Confirmed contact before a job goes live
parts.what: Requires a phone number or email confirmed with the kit's checks before a customer's first job goes live, so workers know it is real.

parts.name: Customer age rules
parts.what: Customers under 18 can post only small jobs, and those are paid through held stages like any other job, never the less protected path; what a person under 18 may agree to is checked against the contract law for minors first, with a parent or carer linked where needed.

features.name: Sign up as a worker
features.does: A tradesperson or freelancer can join, choose their trades or skills and areas, and start quoting.

parts.name: Worker onboarding steps
parts.what: Guided steps for business details, trades, areas, licences and payout account, saved as the worker goes.

parts.name: Trade and skill picker
parts.what: Picks trades and skills from the shared category tree, with search.

parts.name: Identity check
parts.what: Sends the worker to the kit's identity check and keeps only the verified name and date of birth, which licence matching uses.

parts.name: Own-business questions
parts.what: Asks and records that the worker runs their own business and sets their own prices and hours.

parts.name: Payout account set-up
parts.what: Puts the kit's payout set-up into the onboarding steps; a worker can quote before it is done but cannot be paid until it is.

parts.name: Business check
parts.what: Confirms a worker's business through the kit's business number lookup (example: the NZ Business Number) and keeps its trader details, so customers see the legal entity behind each quote.

parts.name: Worker age rules
parts.what: A minimum age for each category: a teenager can offer simple jobs such as lawn mowing with a parent or carer linked, while licensed work, childcare and work with held money are for adults only; young workers also get the hazardous-work limits, such as, in New Zealand, no ride-on mowers or other heavy machinery under 15 (confirm the rule in the health and safety regulations).

parts.name: Right to work
parts.what: Uses the kit's visa entitlement check at sign-up and re-checks before a visa lapses, since many work visas tie a person to one employer and do not allow contracting on the side.

features.name: Hire and work from one account
features.does: One person can hire and work from the same account and switch views.

parts.name: Roles on one account
parts.what: Declares Spare Work's customer, worker and business roles on the kit's roles per app.

parts.name: Role switcher
parts.what: Switches between the customer view and the worker view in one tap.

features.name: Business customer accounts
features.does: A company, landlord, school or property manager can hire with several staff, spending limits and approvals.

parts.name: Business customer roles
parts.what: Spare Work's roles on the kit's organisation model: requester, approver, site contact and accounts, and who may approve spending.

parts.name: Spending limits and approvals
parts.what: Jobs over a set amount wait for a named approver before a quote is accepted.

parts.name: Purchase order numbers and cost codes
parts.what: Adds purchase order numbers, sites and cost codes to jobs and invoices.

parts.name: Monthly statement for businesses
parts.what: One monthly statement of all jobs, stages and invoices for an organisation.

features.name: Sign in safely
features.does: A member can sign in on any device with the kit's sign-in, and payouts stay safe after a lost account is recovered.

parts.name: Kit sign-in in Spare Work
parts.what: Uses the kit's passkeys, second sign-in step, sessions and account recovery; Spare Work requires the second step for workers and pauses payouts for a safe period after a recovery.

features.name: Pause or close an account
features.does: A member can pause taking work, or close their account and take their data with them.

parts.name: Pause availability
parts.what: Hides a worker from matching and search while they are away, without losing anything.

parts.name: Close with open-job checks
parts.what: Closing waits until held money, open stages and disputes are settled, offers a data export first, and ends the person's Spare Work membership, unless they are still a member through another app.

parts.name: When a sole trader dies
parts.what: Uses the kit's after-death handling, so an estate's named contact can close the account, settle held money for work done and hand open jobs to a replacement worker.

areas.name: Profiles, portfolios and credentials
areas.summary: Worker profiles that show checked facts: licences matched against public registers, insurance, past jobs done on the platform, and a portfolio.

features.name: Build a worker profile
features.does: A worker can show their business name, trades, areas served, about text, hours and how to reach them.

parts.name: Profile data model
parts.what: Business details, trades, skills, areas, hours and credentials for each worker or business.

parts.name: Profile editor
parts.what: Edits every part of the profile, with a preview of what customers see.

parts.name: Public profile page
parts.what: The page customers see, with credentials, reviews, facts and portfolio.

parts.name: Areas served
parts.what: Draws areas on a map or picks suburbs and towns, with a travel distance.

features.name: Show a portfolio
features.does: A worker can add photos, videos, documents and past projects, including jobs done on Spare Work.

parts.name: Portfolio items
parts.what: Portfolio entries with media, a description, trade and rough cost.

parts.name: Job and portfolio media
parts.what: Spare Work's photo and video settings on the kit's file uploads: phone-sized copies, location data stripped from every copy others see, and a prompt to describe each image; for job evidence, the capture time and place are kept privately in the evidence store for disputes.

parts.name: Add a finished job
parts.what: Turns a finished Spare Work job into a portfolio entry once the customer agrees.

parts.name: Copied portfolio checks
parts.what: Checks new portfolio photos against photos already on Spare Work, and sends any match, or a firm's report that its work is shown by someone else, to a person to review.

features.name: Prove licences and registrations
features.does: A worker can link a licence or registration, and customers see it checked against the public register with its expiry date.

parts.name: Which trade and professional registers can be checked
parts.what: Which trade and professional registers have public lookups, their terms and how often to re-check, as Spare Work's input to the kit's register checks.

parts.name: Registers each trade needs
parts.what: Declares to the kit's register checks which registers each trade needs in each country, starting with New Zealand's registers for licensed building practitioners, electrical workers, and plumbers, gasfitters and drainlayers.

parts.name: Re-checks and expiry alerts
parts.what: Uses the kit's re-check scheduler and adds a fresh check before each licensed stage starts.

parts.name: Lapsed licence on open jobs
parts.what: Tells the customer and pauses licensed stages if the named licence holder's licence lapses during a job, with the option to replace the worker.

parts.name: Licence rules per trade
parts.what: Which work needs which licence, registration or licence class, as an open rules table per country, covering, in the New Zealand pack, restricted building work, the other trades and the professions in WORK-A2-F3-P7, with exemptions such as the owner-builder exemption for restricted building work and the homeowner exemption for some electrical work.

parts.name: Credential badges
parts.what: Shows each credential on profiles and quotes with the kit's verified badge, the date checked, the licence class and a link to the register.

parts.name: Professional and other registers
parts.what: Adds the registers for lawyers and conveyancers, registered valuers, real estate licensees, engineers, architects, cadastral surveyors, immigration advisers, financial advice providers, asbestos removal licence holders and security staff, within each register's terms.

parts.name: Match the licence to the person
parts.what: Matches the name and details on each register entry to the worker's identity check, so nobody can quote someone else's licence number; a mismatch goes to a person to review.

parts.name: Named licence holder on each stage
parts.what: Each licensed stage names the licensed person doing or supervising it, with their licence class, so unlicensed crew can work under supervision and the record of work comes from that person.

parts.name: Licence holder is the one signed in
parts.what: Uses the kit's repeat identity checks before a licensed stage starts and when the named licence holder signs off their work, so a licensed account cannot be lent to unlicensed crew.

features.name: Show insurance and memberships
features.does: A worker can add public liability insurance and trade association memberships, checked by a person where no lookup exists.

parts.name: Documents with expiry
parts.what: Uploads a certificate with its expiry date and reminds the worker to renew it.

parts.name: Manual check queue
parts.what: Spare Work's rules for checking documents that have no public lookup, such as insurance certificates, on the kit's review queue; a shared document check belongs in the kit, since hosts and vehicles need it too.

parts.name: Association membership lookups
parts.what: Checks trade association membership where the association offers an open lookup.

features.name: Background checks
features.does: A worker can choose to show that they passed a criminal record check, with their consent; for care work and work with children it is required.

parts.name: Background check options
parts.what: Which Spare Work categories need the kit's safety check: required for care in the home, childcare, tutoring and any other work with children before those categories open, optional for others such as cleaning inside homes, and how to show the result fairly.

parts.name: Background check badge
parts.what: Shows the check type and date with the kit's verified badge, never the details.

features.name: Freelancer skills and qualifications
features.does: A remote worker can show skills, languages, qualifications and optional skill tests.

parts.name: Skills and languages
parts.what: Skills and spoken languages on the profile, from the shared category tree.

parts.name: Qualification check
parts.what: Uploads a qualification for a person to check.

parts.name: Open skill tests
parts.what: Optional skill tests written and reviewed by member workers, published openly.

features.name: Plain performance facts
features.does: A customer can see plain facts: jobs done, on-time stages, response time and repeat customers.

parts.name: Spare Work facts for the reputation summary
parts.what: Spare Work's facts for the kit's reputation summary: jobs done, on-time stages, response time and repeat customers, each worked out from real job records, never from claims.

parts.name: Facts panel
parts.what: Shows the kit's reputation summary on the profile with Spare Work's facts, and how each one is worked out.

features.name: Show a verified ownership tag
features.does: A business owned by a group that buyers' procurement targets favour (example: Māori- or Pasifika-owned businesses in New Zealand) can choose to show a verified tag, for business customers with progressive procurement targets.

parts.name: Ownership tag check
parts.what: Checks the tag against an existing supplier-diversity register, with the business's consent, and shows it only if the business chooses.

parts.name: Filter for business buyers
parts.what: Lets business customers filter search results by the tag.

areas.name: Posting a job
areas.summary: A customer describes what they need once, with photos, drawings, address, timing and budget, and the job reaches the right workers.

features.name: Describe a job
features.does: A customer can post a job with a title, description, trade, photos, location, timing and rough budget.

parts.name: Job data model
parts.what: A job on the kit's request model, with trade, description, media, place, timing, budget and visibility.

parts.name: Job posting form
parts.what: Guided questions per trade, so workers get what they need to quote.

parts.name: Photos and video on a job
parts.what: Adds photos and short videos to a job from the phone camera, with a prompt to describe each image.

parts.name: Address privacy
parts.what: Uses the kit's approximate location: only the suburb shows to everyone, and the exact address only to workers the customer chooses.

parts.name: Roles on a job
parts.what: Names who pays, who approves, the owner for consent and the record of work, and the site contact who lets the worker in, so an adult child, a body corporate, a landlord or an insurer can each play their part.

parts.name: Disclosed commissions and markups
parts.what: When the person who approves a job is not the one who pays, such as a property manager, body corporate manager or insurer's agent, they must disclose any commission, referral fee or markup they get from the job, and the payer sees it on the quote and invoice, as the law on secret commissions expects (example: New Zealand's Secret Commissions Act 1910).

features.name: Pick the right trade
features.does: A customer can pick the right trade or service from a clear list, or have one suggested from their description.

parts.name: Category tree
parts.what: Trades and services as open data, in many languages, with plain names.

parts.name: Suggest a category
parts.what: Suggests a category from the description for the customer to confirm, using a model run at cost.

parts.name: Category changes by vote
parts.what: New or changed categories are proposed and voted on by members.

features.name: Attach drawings and documents
features.does: A customer can attach plans, Spare Construct drawings, building consent documents and specifications.

parts.name: Document attachments and viewer
parts.what: Attaches PDFs and images and views them on any device.

parts.name: Spare Construct drawing links
parts.what: Links a Spare Construct drawing set through Spare Construct's public command API, never a code dependency or the AI channel.

parts.name: Building consent details
parts.what: Records the consent number, the council and the consent documents on the job.

parts.name: Does it need consent?
parts.what: Plain guidance on whether work needs a building consent or is exempt under the country's building law (example: Schedule 1 of New Zealand's Building Act, including the small stand-alone dwelling exemption), with a link to the council.

features.name: Help with scoping
features.does: A customer can see a rough price range and a checklist of what to ask before posting.

parts.name: Price ranges from past jobs
parts.what: Price ranges by trade and region from finished jobs, published as open data only for groups large enough that no customer or worker can be identified.

parts.name: Scoping checklists
parts.what: Short checklists per trade written by member workers.

parts.name: Licensed work notice
parts.what: Tells the customer in plain words when the job needs a licensed or registered person, and matches only workers who hold it.

features.name: Choose who sees the job
features.does: A customer can send a job to all matching workers, to a shortlist, or straight to one worker they know.

parts.name: Open, invited or direct
parts.what: Visibility settings for a job: open to matching workers, invited only, or direct to one worker.

parts.name: Invite by link
parts.what: Invites a named worker, already on Spare Work or not, with a link; an invite to someone who is not a member carries a named sender and one-step unsubscribe, as spam law asks.

features.name: Manage a posted job
features.does: A customer can edit, pause, close or repost a job and see who has responded.

parts.name: Job states and history
parts.what: Draft, open, quoting, agreed, in progress, done, paid outside the app and closed, each change an operation on the kit's order steps.

parts.name: Customer job page
parts.what: Shows responses, questions, quotes and next steps for one job.

parts.name: Close stale jobs
parts.what: Reminds the customer and then closes a job nobody has acted on, telling workers.

features.name: Recurring and urgent jobs
features.does: A customer can mark a job as urgent so nearby available workers see it first, or post a repeating job such as monthly lawn mowing.

parts.name: Recurring jobs
parts.what: Repeating jobs on the kit's scheduled and repeat bookings, with the same worker until either side stops.

parts.name: Urgent call-outs
parts.what: Urgent jobs go to available workers nearby first, with any call-out charge shown upfront.

parts.name: Danger first
parts.what: For a gas smell, live wires or flooding, shows the emergency number (111 in New Zealand) and the gas or lines company's emergency number before any matching starts.

features.name: Know what work can be offered
features.does: A customer and a worker can see which services may never be offered, and which need a licence, registration or age check, before posting.

parts.name: Reserved and prohibited services law
parts.what: Every law in each country that reserves work to licensed people or bans a service, with sources, starting with New Zealand's: lawyers' reserved areas, immigration advice, real estate agency, financial advice, security work, asbestos removal, health practitioners' restricted activities and protected titles, veterinary work, auctioneers (registration under the Auctioneers Act 2013), debt collection and repossession, food businesses under the Food Act 2014 such as private chefs and caterers, passenger services (a small passenger service licence), goods moved for hire in heavier vehicles (a goods service licence), and contract cheating (an offence under the Education and Training Act 2020, reported as s393; confirm the section).

parts.name: Service rules as data
parts.what: Banned, restricted and licence-needed services as versioned rules linked to categories and keywords, changed by member vote.

parts.name: Checks on jobs and services
parts.what: Checks each job, service and quote against the rules: blocks banned work such as fake reviews, contract cheating and payment agent jobs that move money for others, and asks for the licence where the work needs one.

parts.name: Rules pages
parts.what: Plain pages listing what can and cannot be offered and why.

parts.name: Remote services stay within one country at first
parts.what: Until the sales tax rule for remote services from overseas workers is live (WORK-A11-F6-P3), remote services such as a logo or a report are bought and sold only between people resident in the same country, so no overseas worker sells to a consumer in another country through the co-op.

parts.name: Boundaries with other programs
parts.what: Which program owns overlapping work, agreed with Spare Ride, Food, Stay and Rent: rides and courier deliveries belong to Spare Ride or Spare Food and property management to Spare Rent, and Spare Work blocks or redirects those jobs, so 'drive me to the airport' never becomes an unlicensed passenger service.

parts.name: Care work waits for safety checks
parts.what: Childcare, care in the home, tutoring and any other work with children stay out of the first release, and open only with the kit's safety check required for every worker in them.

features.name: Describe a job by voice
features.does: A customer who cannot type easily can describe a job by speaking and check the text before posting.

parts.name: Voice to text for jobs
parts.what: Turns a spoken description into text with a model run at cost, for the customer to check and edit.

features.name: Rebuild after a disaster
features.does: After a flood or storm, a region can switch to disaster mode, with urgent safety work first, insurer-funded jobs and fair prices.

parts.name: Disaster mode
parts.what: A region switch on the kit's feature switches, set by a logged emergency action, that puts urgent safety jobs first and opens insurer-funded jobs; a shared emergency mode belongs in the kit, since Spare Ride, Stay and Market need the same switch.

parts.name: Workers from other regions
parts.what: Lets workers from other regions serve the region, with licences and identity checked as usual before any quote.

parts.name: Price guidance against gouging
parts.what: Shows the customer the region's normal price range next to each quote, as guidance only.

areas.name: Finding work and matching
areas.summary: Workers see jobs that fit their trades, areas and licences, for free. No paid leads, no tokens to quote, no paid placement.

features.name: Job feed for workers
features.does: A worker can browse open jobs that fit their trades, areas and licences, at no cost.

parts.name: Job feed with filters
parts.what: Lists matching jobs with filters for trade, distance, budget and timing.

parts.name: Map of jobs
parts.what: Shows jobs on a map at suburb level, never the exact address.

parts.name: Saved searches
parts.what: Spare Work's job filters saved with the kit's saved searches, alerting on new jobs that fit.

features.name: Fair matching
features.does: The platform sends each job to workers who fit, fairly, and nobody can pay to be seen first.

parts.name: Work matching rules
parts.what: Spare Work's scoring rules as a plugin to the kit's matching: trade, area, licence and capacity only; declining a job never lowers a worker's place.

parts.name: Fair rotation
parts.what: Rotates who sees each job first, so new and small workers are seen and not only the busiest, checked by the kit's fairness checks.

parts.name: Cap on quotes per job
parts.what: Limits how many workers can quote one job, never below the customer protection floor, so customers are not flooded and workers do not waste time.

parts.name: Published matching rules
parts.what: Publishes Spare Work's matching rules and their voted values through the kit's published ranking and offer rules; no paid placement anywhere.

parts.name: Explain and review automated decisions
parts.what: Every automated decision about a worker's income, such as rotation, quote caps, auto-release, fraud holds and pauses, comes with a plain reason and a human review on request, and never uses grounds the law forbids.

parts.name: Automated decisions in the AI register
parts.what: Lists each automated or AI decision Spare Work makes, such as category suggestions, rotation, quote caps, auto-release, fraud holds, fake review flags and copied photo checks, in the co-op's AI use register with what each may decide.

features.name: Job alerts
features.does: A worker can get push, email or text alerts for new jobs that fit them.

parts.name: Alert rules and quiet hours
parts.what: Chooses which jobs trigger an alert and when alerts stay silent.

parts.name: Daily digest
parts.what: One summary a day instead of single alerts.

features.name: Show interest and ask questions
features.does: A worker can say they are interested, ask the customer questions or ask for a site visit before quoting.

parts.name: Interest, then choose
parts.what: The worker shows interest and the customer chooses who to talk to, before details are shared; the flow and its name are our own, checked under WORK-A4-F4-P4.

parts.name: Shared questions
parts.what: Questions and answers on a job, shown to all quoting workers when the customer allows.

parts.name: Decline with a reason
parts.what: A worker can pass on a job with a quick reason that helps the customer re-scope it.

parts.name: Intellectual property check
parts.what: Searches the IPONZ patent register and others before design, since a trades site we replace markets a similar two-step connection flow.

features.name: Invitations to quote
features.does: A worker can receive a direct invitation to quote and accept or decline it.

parts.name: Invitation inbox
parts.what: Lists invitations with accept and decline, and tells the customer the answer.

features.name: Capacity and availability
features.does: A worker can set how much work they can take and when, so they only see jobs they can do.

parts.name: Capacity settings
parts.what: Sets how many jobs at once, lead time and a booked-out mode.

parts.name: Matching honours capacity
parts.what: Matching skips workers who are booked out until their chosen date.

features.name: Subcontract and team up
features.does: A worker can find other trades to subcontract to or team up with on a bigger job.

parts.name: Worker-to-worker jobs
parts.what: A worker can post a job for other workers, such as a main contractor finding a tiler.

parts.name: Joint quotes
parts.what: Several workers quote one job together on the kit's multi-party orders, each with their own stages and payouts.

areas.name: Finding a worker
areas.summary: Customers can search and browse workers directly by trade, place, checked licences, reviews and price, and compare them side by side.

features.name: Search for workers
features.does: A customer can search for workers by trade or skill, place, licence and rating.

parts.name: Profile search index
parts.what: Spare Work's profile and service fields indexed in the kit's search service, kept current from the operation log.

parts.name: Search page with filters
parts.what: Search with filters for trade, distance, credentials, rating and availability.

parts.name: Search in many languages
parts.what: Finds the right trade whatever language the customer searches in.

parts.name: Harvest limits
parts.what: Spare Work's limits on the kit's bulk copy and traffic limits for search, directory pages and the API, so nobody can harvest sole traders' phone numbers, addresses or reviews in bulk.

features.name: Trades directory
features.does: A customer can browse a directory of trades by region, such as plumbers in a given town.

parts.name: Directory pages
parts.what: Directory pages built from profiles, fast to load and readable by search engines, within the harvest limits.

parts.name: Regions and suburbs
parts.what: Region, town and suburb names from open address data.

features.name: Compare workers
features.does: A customer can compare the workers who responded side by side: price, reviews, credentials and availability.

parts.name: Comparison view
parts.what: Side-by-side view of responding workers and their quotes.

features.name: Save and rehire
features.does: A customer can save favourite workers and send a new job straight to them.

parts.name: Favourites
parts.what: Saved workers on the kit's favourites, private to the customer.

parts.name: Rehire
parts.what: Starts a direct job to a past worker with details filled in from the last job.

features.name: Related trades
features.does: A customer can see which other trades a job usually needs, such as a plasterer after an electrician.

parts.name: Related-trade rules
parts.what: Links between trades from the category tree, shown as suggestions, never paid placement.

areas.name: Fixed-price services
areas.summary: Workers can sell set services at a set price, such as a building inspection, a gas safety check or a logo, bought in a few taps.

features.name: List a service
features.does: A worker can list a service with a description, price, delivery time and what is included.

parts.name: Service listing model
parts.what: A listed service with scope, price, time, area and category, on the shared marketplace engine.

parts.name: Listing editor
parts.what: Writes and previews a service listing with photos and samples.

parts.name: Entries in the shared service catalogue
parts.what: Publishes Spare Work's services as entries in one shared service catalogue on the kit's marketplace engine, so Spare Home and Spare Stay book the same pro with one account, one set of checks and one reputation; the catalogue belongs in the kit and is not yet on the kit's map.

features.name: Packages and extras
features.does: A worker can offer up to three packages and paid add-ons such as faster delivery or more revisions.

parts.name: Package and extras pricing
parts.what: Package tiers and add-ons with their own prices and times.

parts.name: Package comparison
parts.what: Shows packages side by side on the listing.

features.name: Buy a service
features.does: A customer can buy a listed service, answer the worker's set questions and pay into a held account.

parts.name: Service checkout
parts.what: Checkout for listed services using held payments.

parts.name: Set questions
parts.what: Questions the worker needs answered before starting, asked at checkout.

parts.name: Book a time for on-site services
parts.what: Picks a time slot from the worker's calendar for services done on site.

features.name: Custom offers
features.does: A worker can send one customer a one-off offer with its own price, time and stages.

parts.name: Custom offer
parts.what: A one-off offer built from the quote model and sent in a message; an offer the customer did not ask for carries the uninvited direct sale notice.

features.name: Browse services
features.does: A customer can browse and search services by category, price and delivery time.

parts.name: Service search and pages
parts.what: Search and category pages for listed services.

features.name: Revisions and delivery
features.does: A customer can use the revisions included, accept the final delivery, or cancel if it comes late.

parts.name: Revision counter and acceptance
parts.what: Tracks revisions used and releases payment when the delivery is accepted.

parts.name: Cancel when late
parts.what: A buyer can cancel and get the held money back when a fixed-price service is late, unless the buyer caused the delay.

features.name: Paid consultations
features.does: A customer can book a short paid call or site visit for advice before deciding on a job.

parts.name: Consultation booking
parts.what: Books a consultation slot with the fee held until it happens.

areas.name: Quotes and proposals
areas.summary: Workers quote for free; customers compare quotes, ask questions and accept one. An accepted quote becomes stages with amounts and sign-off conditions.

features.name: Write a quote
features.does: A worker can write a quote with line items, labour, materials, sales tax, exclusions, start date and expiry.

parts.name: Quote, stage and sign-off model
parts.what: Design note with worked examples for a small repair, a renovation and a remote job.

parts.name: Quote data model
parts.what: Spare Work's quote fields, such as line items, labour, materials, exclusions, expiry and proposed stages, as an extension of the kit's offers and quotes and its quote requests.

parts.name: Quote builder
parts.what: Builds a quote on a phone or desktop, from scratch, a template or the price book.

parts.name: Price book
parts.what: The worker's saved items, rates and markups, used across quotes.

parts.name: Tax and totals
parts.what: Works out sales tax and totals from the worker's tax status and the country's rules, using the kit's full price first, so consumers always see tax-inclusive totals.

features.name: Estimate, quote or fixed price
features.does: A worker can mark a price as an estimate, a quote or a fixed price, and the customer sees what each means.

parts.name: Price types
parts.what: Price type rules with a plain explanation shown to the customer.

parts.name: Estimate to quote after a visit
parts.what: Turns an estimate into a firm quote after a site visit, keeping the history.

parts.name: Paid measure-ups for large jobs
parts.what: For a large job, a worker can ask for an agreed fee for a measure-up or design before quoting, shown upfront and credited if the quote is accepted; quoting itself stays free.

features.name: Proposals for remote work
features.does: A freelancer can send a proposal with an approach, timeline, milestones and samples.

parts.name: Proposal form
parts.what: A proposal view of the quote model for remote work.

parts.name: Attach portfolio samples
parts.what: Picks relevant portfolio items to send with a proposal.

features.name: Compare and accept quotes
features.does: A customer can compare quotes line by line, ask questions, and accept one.

parts.name: Quote comparison
parts.what: Line-by-line comparison that lines up similar items and shows what each quote leaves out.

parts.name: Accept or decline
parts.what: Accepts one quote, declines others with an optional reason, and tells every worker.

parts.name: Quote to agreement
parts.what: Turns the accepted quote into a written agreement with stages.

features.name: Revise a quote
features.does: A worker can revise a quote before it is accepted, and the customer sees exactly what changed.

parts.name: Quote versions
parts.what: Keeps every version and shows changes between them.

features.name: Quote templates
features.does: A worker can save quote templates for jobs they do often.

parts.name: Templates
parts.what: Saves a quote as a template and starts new quotes from it.

features.name: Price from drawings
features.does: A worker can price straight from quantities in a Spare Construct drawing set attached to the job.

parts.name: Read quantities
parts.what: Reads quantities from attached drawings through Spare Construct's public command API.

parts.name: Quantities to price book
parts.what: Matches quantities to price book items to start a quote.

features.name: Charge-up jobs
features.does: A trade can work on time and materials, with a rate card, time on site, materials receipts with the markup shown, and an optional cap.

parts.name: Rate card
parts.what: Hourly rates, call-out charge and materials markup, shown to the customer before they agree.

parts.name: Time on site
parts.what: Records time on site with start and stop, or entered after, with notes, as operations the customer can see; hourly remote work uses the same records.

parts.name: Materials with receipts
parts.what: Materials lines with a photo of the receipt and the markup shown.

parts.name: Not-to-exceed cap
parts.what: An optional cap; work pauses for the customer's approval before going over it.

areas.name: Agreements, stages and changes
areas.summary: Every accepted job becomes a written agreement in plain words, with stages, sign-off conditions and a clean way to agree changes.

features.name: Written agreement
features.does: Both sides get a written agreement from the accepted quote, with the terms the law requires.

parts.name: Agreement document
parts.what: Builds the agreement from the quote, both sides' details and the standard terms, as a PDF and a web page.

parts.name: Building law pack (example: New Zealand's Building Act)
parts.what: Each country's rules for building contracts; for New Zealand residential building work: the disclosure statement and checklist before signing when the price is $30,000 or more including GST, or whenever the client asks, and a written contract at $30,000 or more.

parts.name: Plain standard terms
parts.what: Standard terms in plain words, written with a lawyer, with no unfair terms.

parts.name: Confidentiality and ownership terms
parts.what: Optional confidentiality terms and who owns the work once paid, mainly for remote work.

parts.name: Signing
parts.what: The paying party, any named approver and the worker sign in the app through the kit's signatures, with an audit trail and a signed PDF copy for each party.

parts.name: Residential building duties on every job
parts.what: For all residential building work in the New Zealand pack, whatever the price: the implied warranties, the 12-month defect repair period and the information due on completion, shown in the agreement.

parts.name: Worker's own terms
parts.what: A worker can attach their own terms of trade next to the standard terms, with a plain rule for which wins; terms that cut back consumer guarantees or are unfair are blocked.

parts.name: One binding language
parts.what: Each agreement and change names one binding language; translations are marked as translations, so both sides see which text counts.

parts.name: Uninvited direct sales
parts.what: When the worker starts the deal uninvited, such as a custom offer, a yearly service reminder with a price, a quote nobody asked for or a door-knock after a storm, the agreement carries the cancellation notice and cooling-off period consumer law requires (example: the Fair Trading Act notice and 5 working days in New Zealand); which flows count is confirmed with a lawyer.

features.name: Stages and sign-off conditions
features.does: A customer and worker can split a job into stages, each with an amount, a due date and what counts as done.

parts.name: Stage model
parts.what: Stages with amounts, dates, sign-off conditions and required evidence.

parts.name: Stage planner
parts.what: Plans and edits stages before signing, with totals that must match the quote.

parts.name: Deposit rules
parts.what: Shows the deposit size and when it is due, including a materials deposit, within a voted cap that never goes above the customer protection floor, once the kit's competition law check allows members to vote on it.

features.name: Agree changes
features.does: Either side can propose a change to scope, price or time, and it applies only once both agree.

parts.name: Variation requests
parts.what: A change request on the kit's order changes, linked to the agreement, with price and time effects; extras found after the work use the kit's extra charges after the job.

parts.name: Variation approval
parts.what: Shows the change side by side with the current agreement and asks for approval.

parts.name: Agreement history
parts.what: Keeps every agreed version with who agreed and when.

features.name: Payment claims
features.does: A worker can make a payment claim for a stage, and the customer can answer with a payment schedule, as construction law expects.

parts.name: Construction payment rules
parts.what: Whether the app's stage invoices count as payment claims under construction contracts law (example: New Zealand's Construction Contracts Act), including for residential occupiers, and the timings and content that follow; settled before stage payments ship.

parts.name: Claim and schedule forms
parts.what: Payment claim and payment schedule forms with the legal wording and deadlines.

parts.name: Deadline reminders
parts.what: Reminds both sides before a claim or schedule deadline passes, counted in working days on the kit's working-day clock.

parts.name: Suspending work after a missed payment
parts.what: Shows a worker their right under construction contracts law (example: New Zealand's Construction Contracts Act) to suspend work after a missed scheduled payment, with the notice it needs, and tells the customer before work stops.

features.name: Cancel an agreement
features.does: Either side can cancel by the agreed rules, with held money returned or released fairly.

parts.name: Cancellation and settlement
parts.what: Spare Work's settlement rule on the kit's cancellation policies: works out what is owed for work done and returns or releases held money.

features.name: Retentions
features.does: A customer or main contractor can hold back a retention that is kept safely and released on time.

parts.name: Retention rules
parts.what: When retentions are allowed and how they must be held in each country, starting with New Zealand commercial contracts and the Construction Contracts Act's trust rules for retention money.

parts.name: Retention tracking
parts.what: Tracks each retention and releases it on the agreed date; retention money is never left with the payment provider, whose holds end long before a 12-month retention does, and is held as the trust rules require.

features.name: Replace a worker mid-job
features.does: A customer can replace a worker who abandons the job, becomes insolvent, dies or loses their licence, without losing the job's history.

parts.name: Settle the part done
parts.what: Settles held money for work done to date, with a member panel deciding if the sides cannot agree.

parts.name: Record of work for the part done
parts.what: Asks the named licence holder, or their firm or estate, for a record of work for the part done.

parts.name: Re-tender the rest
parts.what: Re-posts the remaining stages with the job history, drawings and inspections attached.

areas.name: Held payments and payouts
areas.summary: Money for each stage is held by a regulated payment provider, released when the stage is signed off, and the worker keeps everything except the at-cost fee.

features.name: Fund a stage
features.does: A customer can pay a stage into a held account by card or bank payment before the work starts.

parts.name: Holding stage payments legally
parts.what: How held stage payments must be run, building on Spare Kit piece K02.

parts.name: Held funds per stage
parts.what: Maps each Spare Work stage onto the kit's stage payments, linked to the stage as an operation.

parts.name: Payment screen
parts.what: Spare Work's view of the kit's checkout: the stage, the amount, the fee and where the money is held.

parts.name: Held money on the job
parts.what: Shows each stage's money as held, released or refunded, with dates.

parts.name: Fund each stage just in time
parts.what: Asks the customer to pay a stage in shortly before it starts, releases or refunds it within the provider's hold limit (90 days for Stripe outside the US), and captures or renews card holds before they expire, so a long job never outlasts a hold.

parts.name: Bank payments for stages
parts.what: Lets a customer fund a stage by bank payment through the kit, the default for large stages where the provider supports it, since card fees of 2.7% + 30c would add about $1,080 to a $40,000 stage.

features.name: Release a stage
features.does: A customer can release a stage when it is done, and the money reaches the worker quickly.

parts.name: Release with sign-off
parts.what: Releases the stage's money when the customer signs it off.

parts.name: Release if no reply
parts.what: Spare Work's settings for the kit's auto-confirm: how many working days after a stage is marked done, with reminders, set by member vote but never below the customer protection floor.

parts.name: Release for materials
parts.what: Releases part of a held stage early when the worker shows proof of buying materials for it, up to the amount agreed.

features.name: Pay without holding
features.does: A customer and worker can skip holding, pay an invoice in the app or on the worker's phone, or record a payment made outside the app.

parts.name: Pay an invoice
parts.what: Pays a worker's invoice straight through the payment provider.

parts.name: Holding threshold
parts.what: Holding is on by default above a size set by member vote, never above the customer protection floor's maximum.

parts.name: Paid outside the app
parts.what: Records that the customer paid by bank transfer or cash, confirmed by the worker, so reviews, the completion pack, defect tracking and records still work.

parts.name: Take a card on site
parts.what: Takes a card on the worker's phone at the end of a job through the payment provider's tap to pay, with the kit's card fee check applied, since a surcharge ban may cover in-person payments; needs card-present payments added to the kit.

features.name: See the fee
features.does: Both sides can see the at-cost fee on every job and what it paid for.

parts.name: Fee calculation
parts.what: Spare Work's fee on the kit's fee calculator and fee setting, counting the jobs and costs that the fee basis sets.

parts.name: Fee shown everywhere
parts.what: Shows the kit's fee breakdown on Spare Work quotes, stage payments, invoices and payouts.

parts.name: Fee basis when money stays outside
parts.what: Decides how matching, licence re-checks, messages, panels and support are paid for on jobs paid outside the app: a small fee on accepted agreements, or a fee only on paid jobs with the gap shown; settled before the first fee is set.

parts.name: Gap shown on the ledger
parts.what: Shows on Spare Work's ledger page what jobs paid outside the app cost to support and who covered it.

parts.name: Interest on held money
parts.what: Whether held money earns interest or another benefit for the provider or the co-op, who gets it, and how it is shown on the ledger at cost.

features.name: Refunds
features.does: A customer can get held money back when a stage is cancelled or a dispute goes their way, and a worker knows where they stand if a card is charged back.

parts.name: Refunds and part refunds
parts.what: Part refunds by stage on the kit's refunds, recorded against the stage.

parts.name: Chargeback rules
parts.what: Spare Work's choices under the kit's loss rules when a card is charged back after a stage is released: who bears the loss, recovery from later payouts within limits, and protection for workers whose customer signed off first.

parts.name: Chargeback evidence from the workroom
parts.what: Sends the agreement, sign-off, photos and messages from the workroom with the kit's answer to a card dispute.

features.name: Tips and bonuses
features.does: A customer can add a tip or bonus, and the worker gets all of it except the payment provider's own charge on it, shown before paying.

parts.name: Tips
parts.what: Turns on the kit's tips for Spare Work jobs: no co-op fee is taken, and only the provider's own charge on the tip comes off, shown before the customer pays.

features.name: Payments across countries
features.does: A customer and worker in different countries can work together with clear currency conversion.

parts.name: Many currencies
parts.what: Spare Work's held stages and payouts in the kit's currencies for each country.

parts.name: Exchange rate shown first
parts.what: Shows the exchange rate and any conversion cost before paying.

features.name: Payout history
features.does: A worker can see every payout, fee and refund, and download statements.

parts.name: Payouts and statements
parts.what: Spare Work's view of the kit's earnings page and yearly statement, linking each payout to its job and stage, with a tax invoice for the fee.

features.name: Jobs paid by an insurer
features.does: An insurer, or the Natural Hazards Commission, can pay the worker directly while the owner pays any excess and approves the work.

parts.name: Insurer as payer
parts.what: Lets a job name an insurer as payer for agreed stages, with the owner paying the excess and approving the work.

parts.name: Insurance repair jobs
parts.what: How insurers and the Natural Hazards Commission authorise and pay for repairs, and what they need from the worker.

features.name: Pay for a large job in instalments
features.does: A customer can pay a large job over time through a regulated lender, with the full cost of credit shown first.

parts.name: Credit law check
parts.what: What consumer credit law and the buy now, pay later rules ask of a platform that offers a lender's finance (example: New Zealand's Credit Contracts and Consumer Finance Act), settled before any is offered.

parts.name: Lender link
parts.what: Offers finance from a regulated lender at checkout for large stages; the lender pays into the held stage and the co-op takes no commission.

areas.name: Doing the job
areas.summary: Each job has one place for its schedule, site visits, messages, files, progress photos, deliveries and sign-offs.

features.name: Job workroom
features.does: Both sides can see the agreement, stages, money, messages, files and next steps for a job in one place.

parts.name: Workroom page
parts.what: One page per job with the agreement, stages, held money, messages and files.

parts.name: Job timeline
parts.what: Spare Work's events on the kit's order timeline.

parts.name: Next step prompts
parts.what: Tells each side what they need to do next and by when.

features.name: Book a site visit
features.does: A worker can offer times for a site visit and the customer picks one.

parts.name: Site visit booking
parts.what: Offers time slots from the worker's calendar and books one.

parts.name: Address and access notes
parts.what: Shares the exact address, parking and access notes only once a visit is booked.

parts.name: Visit reminders and running late
parts.what: Reminds both sides and lets the worker say they are running late in one tap.

parts.name: No-shows and call-out fees
parts.what: Uses the kit's no-show policies for site visits on either side, with any call-out fee agreed before the visit.

parts.name: On my way
parts.what: The worker sends an 'on my way' message with an arrival time, and their live location is shared only until they arrive.

features.name: Schedule the work
features.does: A worker can set start and stage dates, and the customer sees any change.

parts.name: Job schedule
parts.what: Stage dates on the shared calendar, with changes sent to the customer and shared through the kit's calendar export.

features.name: Share progress
features.does: A worker can post progress photos and notes for each stage.

parts.name: Progress updates
parts.what: Photos and notes linked to a stage.

parts.name: Evidence photo checks
parts.what: Prefers progress photos taken in the app, with their time and place kept as evidence, and checks stage photos for reuse from other jobs or the web and for signs of editing, sending any match to a person to review.

features.name: Deliver work
features.does: A remote worker can deliver files, and a trade can mark a stage as done with evidence.

parts.name: Deliveries
parts.what: Delivers files and notes against a stage.

parts.name: Completion evidence
parts.what: Photos, certificates of compliance, electrical safety and test certificates, and producer statements attached to a stage as the kit's proof of handover.

parts.name: Record of work
parts.what: In the New Zealand pack, the named licensed building practitioner gives the owner and the council a record of work when restricted building work is done, or when they stop work, as Building Act s88 requires; whether this now covers small stand-alone dwellings built without consent is unverified.

parts.name: Preview deliveries
parts.what: A remote worker can deliver a preview or watermarked copy; the full files and ownership pass when the stage is released.

parts.name: How it was made
parts.what: A worker says whether a delivery was made with AI tools, shown on the delivery and in the portfolio.

features.name: Sign off a stage
features.does: A customer can sign off a stage, ask for fixes, or raise a concern.

parts.name: Sign-off and fix requests
parts.what: Signs off a stage, asks for listed fixes with a date, or raises a concern.

parts.name: Completion pack
parts.what: Collects certificates, the record of work, the code compliance certificate once issued, warranties, manuals and the final invoice for the owner to keep.

parts.name: Sign-off by more than one party
parts.what: When a job names several parties, such as a tenant and a landlord, each confirms completion, and the job says whose sign-off releases the money.

features.name: Meet online
features.does: A customer and freelancer can hold a video call from the workroom.

parts.name: Video calls
parts.what: Calls through the kit's call service, never recorded unless both agree.

features.name: Council inspections and sign-off
features.does: A customer and worker can see council inspections in the schedule and track the code compliance certificate at the end.

parts.name: Inspection stages
parts.what: Adds the council's inspections from the consent to the stage schedule, so stage dates follow them.

parts.name: Code compliance certificate
parts.what: Tracks the owner's application for the code compliance certificate and adds it to the completion pack once issued.

areas.name: Hourly and remote work
areas.summary: Remote and hourly work such as design, writing and software, with time records the client can check, weekly billing and work across borders.

features.name: Hourly agreements
features.does: A client can hire at an hourly rate with a weekly hour limit.

parts.name: Hourly terms
parts.what: Hourly agreements with a rate, weekly cap and billing day.

features.name: Log time
features.does: A freelancer can log time by hand or with a timer, with notes for each entry.

parts.name: Time entries
parts.what: Time entries for remote work on the same time records as charge-up jobs, with notes and the stage or task they belong to.

parts.name: Timer and manual entry
parts.what: Starts and stops a timer or adds time by hand, on phone or desktop.

parts.name: Optional desktop tracker
parts.what: A desktop tracker that shares only what the worker chooses, never secret screenshots.

features.name: Review and approve time
features.does: A client can review weekly time and approve or query it before payment.

parts.name: Weekly timesheet
parts.what: Shows the week's entries for the client to approve or query.

parts.name: Weekly billing
parts.what: Charges approved time each week through held payments.

parts.name: Contested hours
parts.what: A client can query entries within a set time; what counts as evidence, such as delivered work and notes, is published, and a contested week goes to the dispute flow.

parts.name: Weekly cap paid in advance
parts.what: The client funds each week's cap into held money shortly before the week starts, within the provider's hold limits, so approved time is paid even if a card fails later.

features.name: Milestone projects
features.does: A client and freelancer can run a remote project with milestones on the same stage flow as trades.

parts.name: Milestones are stages
parts.what: Remote milestones reuse the stage model, deliveries and sign-off.

features.name: Ongoing work
features.does: A client can keep working with a freelancer under one ongoing agreement with weekly or monthly payments.

parts.name: Retainers
parts.what: Ongoing agreements on the kit's regular payments, with notice to stop.

features.name: Work across borders
features.does: A client in one country can hire a freelancer in another, with the right tax forms and rules for both.

parts.name: Cross-border tax details
parts.what: Collects the tax details each country needs from both sides.

parts.name: Sanctions checks
parts.what: Uses the kit's sanctions screening for every cross-border job and payout.

parts.name: Sales tax on remote services from overseas (example: New Zealand GST)
parts.what: When an overseas worker sells remote services to a consumer, the marketplace is often treated as the supplier and must register, charge and return sales tax, as in New Zealand (GST), the EU, the UK and Australia; live before any overseas worker sells to consumers in another country. Confirm the current law in each country.

parts.name: Each side's local time
parts.what: Shows deadlines, weekly billing days and calls in each side's local time.

areas.name: Messages and notifications
areas.summary: Messages between customers and workers tied to each job, plus alerts each member controls.

features.name: Message about a job
features.does: A customer and worker can message about a job, with photos and files.

parts.name: Message threads
parts.what: Spare Work's threads per job and per quote on the kit's chat service.

parts.name: Inbox
parts.what: Groups the kit's chat screens by job and quote, with unread counts and search.

parts.name: Attachments
parts.what: Photos, files and voice notes in messages.

features.name: Share contact details by choice
features.does: A member can share their phone number or email when they choose, and block anyone.

parts.name: Contact sharing
parts.what: Shares contact details only when the member chooses; nothing is hidden to trap people.

parts.name: Off-platform payment warnings
parts.what: Spare Work's wording for the kit's scam warnings when someone asks to pay outside the app: explains the protection lost and never blocks.

parts.name: Block a member
parts.what: Uses the kit's blocking, which also stops the blocked member quoting or inviting.

features.name: Choose notifications
features.does: A member can choose which alerts reach them by push, email or text, and when.

parts.name: Work event list
parts.what: Every work event that can send an alert, such as a new quote or a stage due.

features.name: Saved replies
features.does: A worker can save replies they send often.

parts.name: Saved replies
parts.what: Saves and inserts reply templates.

features.name: Translate messages
features.does: A customer and worker who speak different languages can see messages translated.

parts.name: Message translation
parts.what: Turns on the kit's message translation in job threads, marked as machine translated; agreements follow the binding language rule.

features.name: Call without sharing a number
features.does: A customer can call a worker through the app without showing their own number, if they choose.

parts.name: Masked calls
parts.what: Turns on the kit's masked calls for Spare Work jobs, ending when the job ends.

parts.name: Text or relay service instead of a call
parts.what: A member who is Deaf, hard of hearing or speech-impaired can choose job chat or a relay service call (example: NZ Relay) instead of a masked voice call, and the other side sees how best to reach them; whether masked numbers work through relay services is unverified.

areas.name: Invoices, tax and records
areas.summary: Tax-correct invoices and receipts made from each job, records both sides can keep, and the platform's own reports to the tax office (example: New Zealand's Inland Revenue).

features.name: Send an invoice
features.does: A worker can send a tax-correct invoice made from the agreement and stage, in one tap.

parts.name: Tax invoices and records for trade and freelance work
parts.what: What invoices and records for trade and freelance jobs must show in each country, with sources, starting with New Zealand's, as Spare Work's input to the kit's tax invoices.

parts.name: Invoice generator
parts.what: Maps a stage, a charge-up job or a service onto the kit's tax invoices, as a PDF and open data.

parts.name: Invoice numbering
parts.what: Numbers invoices per worker in order, with credit notes for changes; this belongs in the kit's tax invoices, since every app that issues tax invoices needs it.

parts.name: Tax invoice for the fee
parts.what: Shows the kit's tax invoice for the co-op's fee on each Spare Work payout statement, so workers registered for sales tax can claim it back.

features.name: Keep receipts and records
features.does: A customer can download receipts and a full record of each job for insurance, tax or a house sale.

parts.name: Receipts and job record
parts.what: Issues receipts through the kit's receipts, and exports a full job record as PDF and open data.

parts.name: Records kept for the legal period
parts.what: Spare Work's records on the kit's record keeping and retention schedules, including completion packs owners need after a worker leaves.

parts.name: Records that pass with the property
parts.what: Links each job to its address on a shared property record, so completion packs, records of work, certificates and warranties pass to the next owner when the property is sold, as building law's implied warranties do (example: New Zealand's Building Act); the shared record that Spare Home and Spare Rent map belongs in the kit.

features.name: Set tax status
features.does: A worker can set their sales tax status, and quotes and invoices follow it.

parts.name: Tax rules engine
parts.what: Spare Work's tax cases on the kit's sales tax engine: in New Zealand, trades and freelance work are not listed services, so each worker charges GST by their own status.

parts.name: Sales tax number check
parts.what: Checks the format of a sales tax number (example: a New Zealand GST number) and records the worker's status.

features.name: Platform income reporting
features.does: The co-op reports workers' income to the tax office (example: New Zealand's Inland Revenue) as the digital platform rules for personal services require, and sends each worker a copy.

parts.name: Personal services in the kit's report
parts.what: Feeds Spare Work's personal services income into the kit's yearly report to the tax office and each worker's copy.

features.name: Withholding tax
features.does: A worker can choose a tax rate to be held back from payouts, where the law allows or requires it.

parts.name: Schedular payments and platforms
parts.what: Whether withholding tax rules apply to platform work, and how to offer it as an option.

parts.name: Withholding at payout
parts.what: Holds back the chosen rate at payout and gives a yearly summary.

features.name: Send to accounting software
features.does: A worker can send invoices, payments and fees to their accounting software.

parts.name: Accounting connectors
parts.what: Maps Spare Work invoices, fees and payouts onto the kit's connectors to accounting software.

parts.name: E-invoicing
parts.what: Sends invoices over the open Peppol e-invoicing network; this belongs in the kit beside its tax invoices, for every app that invoices businesses.

features.name: Chase an unpaid invoice
features.does: A worker can set due dates, send reminders and statements, and see the next legal steps when an invoice is overdue.

parts.name: Due dates and reminders
parts.what: Due dates on every invoice, counted in working days where the law asks, polite reminders on a schedule the worker sets, and an overdue status.

parts.name: Statements of account
parts.what: A statement of all open and paid invoices for one customer.

parts.name: Next steps for unpaid work
parts.what: A plain guide to a payment claim under construction contracts law or a small claims tribunal claim (examples: New Zealand's Construction Contracts Act and Disputes Tribunal), with the job record exported.

areas.name: Reviews and reputation
areas.summary: Two-way reviews that only come from real jobs, shown honestly, good and bad, with a fair right of reply.

features.name: Review a worker
features.does: A customer can rate and review a worker after a job, with photos.

parts.name: Review model
parts.what: Spare Work's review categories on the kit's ratings, tied to a finished or cancelled agreement or a job paid outside the app, so only real jobs can be reviewed.

parts.name: Review form
parts.what: Ratings for quality, timing, communication and value, with text and photos.

parts.name: Delays the worker cannot control
parts.what: Adds Spare Work's causes to the kit's rating exclusions, such as weather, council inspections and supplier shortages, so a worker is not marked down for them.

features.name: Review a customer
features.does: A worker can review a customer, so other workers know who communicates well and pays on time, and the customer can reply.

parts.name: Customer reviews
parts.what: Reviews of customers shown to workers deciding whether to quote.

parts.name: Customer's reply, challenge and access
parts.what: A customer can reply to, challenge and see every review about them, and ask for a correction under privacy law.

features.name: See honest reviews
features.does: A customer can see every review, good and bad, and how ratings are worked out.

parts.name: Review display
parts.what: Shows all reviews with the rating maths published.

parts.name: Job size next to each review
parts.what: Shows the job's price band next to each review, such as under $500 or over $50,000, from the agreement, never the exact amount.

features.name: Reply and challenge
features.does: A worker or a customer can reply in public to a review about them and ask for a review that breaks the rules to be checked.

parts.name: Public reply
parts.what: Uses the kit's one reply per review, for workers and customers alike.

parts.name: Review challenge
parts.what: Uses the kit's rating challenge, open to both sides and judged by moderators with no competing business.

features.name: Bring references
features.does: A new worker can show references from past customers, clearly marked as from outside the platform.

parts.name: Reference requests
parts.what: Asks past customers for a reference, shown apart from reviews; each request names the sender and offers one-step unsubscribe, as spam law asks.

features.name: Stop fake reviews
features.does: The platform stops fake, paid and self reviews, and nobody can pay to remove one.

parts.name: Fake review checks
parts.what: Adds Spare Work signals to the kit's fake review checks, such as a reviewer and a worker sharing a card, address or device.

parts.name: Review rules
parts.what: Spare Work's review rules on the kit's fair review rules: no paid removal, no hidden reviews, and removals only under a published rule, logged.

assess: Does every step a customer and a worker take on the incumbents have a home on this map, from first sign-up to the defect repair period?
Is free to quote, always, workable? Which fee basis in WORK-A9-F4-P4 covers the running cost of jobs paid outside the app?
What keeps customers and workers using Spare Work after the first job, without trapping them or hiding contact details?
Which core parts are truly needed for one trade in one region to win and finish real paid work?

Are the licence checks real? Which public registers allow automated lookups under their terms (piece WK02), does each licence match the verified person, and is the licence holder the one signed in before each licensed stage?

Can the payment provider hold stage money long enough? Stripe holds manual payouts for at most 90 days outside the US and offers no escrow. Does funding each stage just in time keep every stage, dispute and appeal inside that limit (piece WK01, WORK-A9-F1-P5), and who bears a chargeback after a stage is released?
Does the contractor design keep workers independent under the 2026 gateway test, and does piece WK03 feed the kit's worker status test (KIT-A23-F1-P1) instead of repeating it?

Is the building law pack for New Zealand correct and current: the disclosure statement and checklist at $30,000 or on request, and the warranties, defect repair period and record of work on every residential job?
Does the quote, stage and sign-off model work for a small repair, a charge-up job, a renovation and a remote design job alike (piece WK04)?
Do Spare Work's stage invoices count as payment claims under construction contracts law (example: New Zealand's Construction Contracts Act)?

Remote work in the first release is limited to people resident in the same country (WORK-A3-F8-P5), while ARCHITECTURE.md leans 'Remote work: Later'. Is that the right line until the sales tax rule for remote services from overseas workers is live?
Is the member dispute panel fair and fast enough, with mediation and inspections first, and who pays for panel members' time?
Are the customer protection floors (WORK-A22-F3-P2) set at the right levels, and who sets them while only workers vote?

Can an agent ever move money, end an agreement, serve a legal notice or share an address without the person (WORK-A19-F2-P2), and can hidden text in a job, quote, review or PDF ever reach an agent as an instruction (WORK-A19-F2-P4)?
Is the at-cost fee shown clearly everywhere money moves, with a tax invoice for it?

What may worker members vote on without breaking competition law (example: New Zealand's Commerce Act)? Does the kit's competition law check (KIT-A12-F4-P3) answer Spare Work's questions on deposit caps and call-out charges (WORK-A18-F3-P3)?
Does anything on the map copy an incumbent's interface, wording or patented process rather than solve the job our own way?
